problem: V16 idle-handoff confirmation is keyed by released session/client hashes but not by the specific released lease epoch. Because one singleton handoff row may be superseded and the same authenticated session/client may legitimately release multiple sequential executions, a delayed acknowledgement for an older release can be indistinguishable from current consent without a generation fence.

owner_contract_consistency: new explicit authenticated interactive work may acquire while a prior handoff is pending

source_observation.inference: Session/client identity is reusable across legal releases; released_lease_epoch is already durable in V16 and is the narrowest available generation fence.

hypothesis: Idle confirmation must be bound to session + client + exact released_lease_epoch, and the clear must be conditional on the same pending epoch, so delayed or duplicated acknowledgements cannot clear a superseding handoff.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Session/client identity alone is sufficient because valid callers will not produce an acknowledgement delayed across two releases by the same session.

mechanism: require positive released_lease_epoch at the public token-ingress confirmation boundary
compare pending session hash + client hash + released lease epoch
return HANDOFF_CONFIRMATION_EPOCH_MISMATCH without clearing on stale generation
clear with a pending-state + epoch conditional update and verify one-row change
preserve explicit-user-priority behavior while autonomous acquisition remains blocked until the current handoff clears

exactly_one_go_oob_experiment.name: ABA_STALE_IDLE_CONFIRMATION_FENCE
exactly_one_go_oob_experiment.design: The same authenticated session/client performs release A, then explicit new work and release B. A delayed confirmation carrying epoch A is submitted after B supersedes the pending row. The discriminator requires rejection, B to remain pending, autonomous acquisition to remain blocked, then allows autonomy only after confirmation carrying epoch B.
exactly_one_go_oob_experiment.purpose: Map the ABA/stale-update generation problem from concurrent systems onto the user-idle handoff without changing owner policy.
